title: Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Elect Obj. 2: Eternal love is not yet actual reconciliation
pass_a_gloss: Objection 2. God is actually reconciled to him whom he actually loves. But he loves all the elect from eternity: Therefore from eternity he is actually reconciled to them: Therefore they also are actually reconciled and justified from eternity. Solution. Distinction must be made with Aquinas. For God is said to love in a twofold way, according to the purpose of communicating his goodness, and according to the very act of communication, In Sentences book 3 distinction 19. That love according to the eternal purpose, which Theologians call the love of eternal benevolence, does not make the one who is loved in this way to be held actually justified or actually reconciled by God, but to be counted among those who are to be infallibly justified and reconciled. There is therefore a diverse account of those words which denote acts immanent in God, and those which denote acts passing from God to us. The former, such as Dilection, Election, Predestination, are eternal and internal acts of God himself; and from them humans are called Beloved, Elect, Predestined, because of the hidden good pleasure of the Divine will conceived and concealed in himself. The latter, such as Calling, Justification, Reconciliation, Glorification, are external acts terminated to an existing creature and as it were received into it; and from them no one is properly called Called, Justified, Reconciled, Glorified from that hidden and eternal purpose of the Divine will alone, but from the accomplished execution of the same purpose and the produced effect in humans. We therefore confess in God an eternal will of justifying and reconciling to himself all the elect: yet we deny that they ought to be said justified or reconciled from eternity: Just as we acknowledge there was in God an eternal will of creating the world, and yet deny that the world was created from eternity. What Zanchi said of the actual remission of sins, that we say of the actual reconciliation of the Elect: It is indeed most certain in the Divine destination from eternity, but it is not given actually on God’s part, nor actually received on the human’s part, until he repents and believes. Thomson, Diatribe page 96.
pass_b_english: Objection 2. God is actually reconciled to whoever he actually loves. He loves every elect person from eternity. So, the objection runs, he has been actually reconciled to them from eternity—and they have been actually reconciled and justified from eternity.

Solution. Follow the distinction in Aquinas. God loves in two senses: by the purpose to communicate his goodness, and by the very act of communicating it (Sentences, book 3, distinction 19). The love that tracks the eternal purpose—theologians call it the love of eternal benevolence—does not already count the beloved as actually justified or actually reconciled. It only ranks that person among those who will infallibly be justified and reconciled. Words for acts that stay inside God, and words for acts that pass from God to us, therefore do different work. Dilection, Election, and Predestination name eternal, inward acts of God; people are called Beloved, Elect, and Predestined from the hidden good pleasure of the divine will conceived and kept in God himself. Calling, Justification, Reconciliation, and Glorification name outward acts that terminate on a creature who already exists and are as it were received into that creature. No one is properly Called, Justified, Reconciled, or Glorified from the hidden eternal purpose alone, but from the finished execution of that purpose and the effect it produces in human beings. We gladly grant that God has an eternal will to justify every elect person and reconcile each to himself. We still refuse to say they were justified or reconciled from eternity. In the same way we grant God an eternal will to create the world, yet deny that the world was created from eternity. What Zanchi said of the actual remission of sins fits the elect's actual reconciliation: it is most certain in the divine destination from eternity, yet it is not actually given on God's side, nor actually received on the human side, before the person repents and believes (Thomson, Diatribe, p. 96).
source_text:
Obj. 2. Deus est illi actu reconciliatus, quem actu diligit. At diligit omnes electos ab aeterno: Ergo ab aeterno est illis actu reconciliatus: Ergo illi sunt etiam actu reconciliati & justificati ab aeterno.

Solut. Distinguendum est cum Aquinate. Deus enim dicitur diligere dupliciter, secundum propositum communicandi bonitatem suam, & secundum ipsum actum communicationis, In 3. Sent. dist. 19. Amor ille secundum aeternum propositum, quem Theologi appellant amorem aeternae benevolentiae, non facit ut qui hunc in modum ametur, actu justificatus, aut actu reconciliatus a Deo habeatur, sed ut inter infallibiliter justificandos & reconciliandos censeatur. Est igitur diversa ratio illorum vocabulorum quae actus in Deo immanentes, & quae actus a Deo ad nos transeuntes denotant. Priora, qualia sunt Dilectio, Electio, Praedestinatio, sunt aeterni & interni actus ipsius Dei; atque ab illis homines dicuntur Dilecti, Electi, Praedestinati, propter arcanum beneplacitum Divinae voluntatis in seipso conceptum & absconditum. Posteriora, qualia sunt Vocatio, Justificatio, Reconciliatio, Glorificatio, sunt actus externi ad creaturam existentem terminati, & in eam quasi recepti; atque ab illis nemo proprie dicitur Vocatus, Justificatus, Reconciliatus, Glorificatus, ex solo illo arcano & aeterno Divinae voluntatis proposito, sed ex facta exsecutione ejusdem propositi, & producto effectu in hominibus. Fatemur ergo in Deo voluntatem aeternam justificandi & sibi reconciliandi omnes electos: negamus tamen eos ab aeterno justificatos aut reconciliatos dici oportere: Sicut agnoscimus fuisse in Deo aeternam voluntatem creandi mundum, & tamen negamus mundum fuisse ab aeterno creatum. Quod Zanch. dixit de remissione actuali peccatorum, id nos dicimus de actuali reconciliatione Electorum: Est quidem illa certissima in destinatione Divina ab aeterno, at actu non datur ex parte Dei, neque actu recipitur ex parte hominis, donec resipiscat & credat. Thomson, Diatr. pag. 96.
